evals.prompt: Get the App Store screenshots for our .NET MAUI app, Sample Recipes (the project is in evals/files/maui-devflow): the plan, a recipe and the shopping list, on iPhone. We've never done store screenshots before.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the project, sees the DevFlow agent registered inside #if DEBUG and the AutomationIds on the tabs, and chooses the devflow driver (saying why: the app already has it, it reaches screens by AutomationId without Appium). It plans dedicated simulators at the required iPhone 6.3" size (1206x2622 from an iPhone 17 Pro) and the 6.9" size (1320x2868 from an iPhone 17 Pro Max), with a clean status bar, demo data and steps by AutomationId; runs capture.py --dry-run first; and checks the full-screen picture includes the status bar.
expectations: The agent notices AddMauiDevFlowAgent inside #if DEBUG (and the package only in Debug) and chooses the devflow driver, giving the reason
The agent confirms the agent is kept out of release builds, or would flag it if it weren't
The capture plan has devices for the required iPhone 6.3" class (1206x2622 or 1179x2556) and, if 6.9" is wanted, 1320x2868, each from a simulator that renders that size natively
The devices are dedicated simulators the skill creates (appstores-<id>), not the user's own
Steps find elements by AutomationId (tab-plan, tab-recipes, tab-shopping) rather than coordinates or text
The plan sets a clean status bar, a fixed clock and a seed, and the agent asks about or proposes fictional demo data
The agent runs capture.py --dry-run and shows or summarises it before the real run
The agent says it will check that each capture is the full screen with the status bar (an in-app window capture may leave it out)

evals.prompt: Our Flutter app (evals/files/flutter-ailoha) needs Google Play phone screenshots. Can you capture them from the Android emulator?
evals.expected_output: The agent sees ailoha_agent in pubspec.yaml and initAgent() under kDebugMode, and chooses the ailoha driver (Flutter's widgets are hard for outside tools to find; the agent sees the real tree). It plans a dedicated emulator with wm size 1080x1920 because every current phone profile is taller than Play's 2:1 limit, uses the Ailoha CLI or its loopback port (9233, adb forward if discovery fails), hides the debug banner, sets demo mode for the status bar, and resets wm size and demo mode afterwards.
expectations: The agent identifies the Ailoha agent (ailoha_agent, initAgent inside kDebugMode) and chooses the ailoha driver, with a reason
The Android device's size is 1080x1920 (or another size within Play's 2:1 limit) set with wmSize on the emulator, not a crop or resize, and the agent says why (phone profiles are about 2.2:1)
The emulator is a dedicated one the skill creates, not a device the user didn't name
The agent mentions the agent's local port (9233 by default) and adb forward if the CLI doesn't find it, or the ailoha CLI's own discovery
The agent mentions hiding Flutter's debug banner (debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false) or other debug UI in the shots
The status bar is cleaned with Android's SystemUI demo mode (9:41 or a fixed time, full battery and signal, no notifications)
The agent says wm size, demo mode and other settings are reset afterwards
Nothing is sent off the machine; the agent talks only to the local emulator and agent

evals.prompt: We already have Appium end-to-end tests (evals/files/appium-suite) for Sample Recipes on iOS and Android. Use them to get store screenshots of the plan, a recipe and the shopping list on both platforms.
evals.expected_output: The agent chooses the appium driver because the suite exists and covers both platforms, reuses its accessibility ids (tab-plan, plan-day-monday, recipe-title, tab-shopping, shopping-list) as the plan's steps, points at a local Appium server on 127.0.0.1:4723, sets each device's exact store size (a simulator that renders the iPhone size natively; an emulator with wm size 1080x1920), applies the status bar override and demo mode outside Appium, and checks the captures' sizes.
expectations: The agent chooses the appium driver and says it's because an Appium suite already reaches these screens on both platforms
The plan's steps reuse the suite's accessibility ids (for example tab-plan, plan-day-monday, recipe-title, tab-shopping, shopping-list) rather than coordinates
The Appium server is local (127.0.0.1 or localhost); the agent doesn't point at a remote grid or cloud
The agent checks or explains how to install the needed Appium drivers (xcuitest, uiautomator2)
The iOS device is a simulator whose native size is a store size, and the Android device uses wm size 1080x1920 (or another size within 2:1)
The status bar is cleaned (simctl status_bar override, Android demo mode) and reset afterwards
The agent doesn't rewrite or replace the user's test suite

evals.prompt: Sample Recipes has a screenshot mode (evals/files/swift-screenshot-mode). Capture the four screens on the required iPhone and iPad sizes in English and German.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the screenshot mode (-ScreenshotScreen, -ScreenshotSeed, Debug only) and chooses the simctl driver with launch arguments (no taps, no test target needed). The plan has dedicated simulators that render the required iPhone 6.3" (1206x2622) and iPad 13" (2064x2752) sizes, screens plan, recipe, shopping and profile each launched with ScreenshotScreen, locales en-US and de-DE, a clean status bar at 9:41; the device language set for German if system UI shows; dry run, run, check_captures.py, and a full-size look at every picture.
expectations: The agent chooses the simctl driver with launch arguments, because the app's screenshot mode reaches every screen without taps
Each screen's step is a launch with args ScreenshotScreen set to plan, recipe, shopping or profile (the seed passed as ScreenshotSeed)
The devices cover the required iPhone 6.3" class (1206x2622 or 1179x2556) and iPad 13" (2064x2752 or 2048x2732), from simulator types that render those sizes natively
The locales are en-US and de-DE; the agent notes the device language matters where system UI shows
The status bar is overridden (9:41, full battery and signal) and verified or flagged per shot
The agent runs capture.py --dry-run before the real run and check_captures.py after
The agent says it will look at every capture at full size (and reports what it saw)
The simulators are dedicated ones the skill creates

evals.prompt: capture.py failed on evals/files/wrong-size/capture-plan.json; the report is evals/files/wrong-size/capture-report.json. The pictures are 828x1792. Just scale them up to 1242x2688 so we can upload them.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the report: the iPhone 11 simulator renders 828x1792, which isn't an accepted App Store size even though the iPhone 11 is listed in the 6.5" class. It declines to upscale (blurry, a store may reject it, and the skill never resizes), and changes the plan's device to a simulator that renders a store size natively: an iPhone 17 Pro (1206x2622, the required 6.3" class) and/or an iPhone 17 Pro Max (1320x2868, 6.9"), or an iPhone 14 Plus / 11 Pro Max for 6.5". Then it captures again and checks.
expectations: The agent does not resize, upscale, crop or pad the 828x1792 pictures, and doesn't write any resized file
The agent explains that the iPhone 11 simulator renders 828x1792, which isn't an accepted size, though the device is listed in Apple's 6.5" class (device names don't promise pixels)
The agent explains why scaling is wrong (blurry or distorted shots; the stores want the app as it looks)

The agent changes the plan's device to a simulator type that renders an accepted size natively (for example iPhone 17 Pro at 1206x2622, iPhone 17 Pro Max at 1320x2868, or iPhone 14 Plus at 1284x2778 / 11 Pro Max at 1242x2688), with width and height to match
The agent mentions that the 6.3" class (1206x2622 or 1179x2556) is the one Apple requires
The agent re-runs capture.py (or says it's next) and check_captures.py

evals.prompt: Google Play rejected our phone screenshots: 'the maximum dimension can't be more than twice the minimum'. The plan is evals/files/android-tall/capture-plan.json. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent sees the medium_phone profile renders 1080x2400 (2.22:1), over Play's 2:1 limit, as every current phone profile is. It sets target.wmSize to 1080x1920 (and a density) so the app lays out at 9:16, Play's recommended size, and the device's width and height to 1080x1920, rather than cropping the pictures; wm size is reset after; then it captures again and checks with check_captures.py --rules google.
expectations: The agent identifies the cause: 1080x2400 is about 2.22:1, over Play's 2:1 limit (common to current phone emulator profiles)
The agent sets target.wmSize to 1080x1920 (or another size within 2:1) and the device's width and height to match
The agent does not crop or resize the existing pictures, and says why (the app wasn't laid out for it; the bars would be cut)
The agent says wm size (and density) are reset after the run
The agent re-captures and runs check_captures.py with Google's rules (or says these are next)

evals.prompt: The capture run finished (report: evals/files/status-bar/capture-report.json). Are these ready to go to the stores?
evals.expected_output: The agent reads every shot's statusBar: en-US iPhone verified (the override was read back from the simulator), de-DE iPhone unverified (the override failed while the simulator rebooted for the language change), Android overridden (demo mode applied, not read back). It doesn't call them ready: none of these values is a check of the pixels, so it looks at each picture's status bar at full size, says the German shot needs a retake with the override applied after the reboot, and checks every shot for transient UI before calling any ready.
expectations: The agent reads the statusBar of every shot and names the de-DE iPhone shot as unverified, with the warning's cause (the override failed during the reboot for the language change)
The agent does not say the set is ready without looking at the pictures
The agent opens (or asks to open) the de-DE shot at full size to look at its status bar, and recommends a retake with the override reapplied after boot
The agent explains that overridden (Android) means applied but not read back, and that even verified means read back from the simulator, not seen in the picture, so it looks at all of them
The agent mentions checking every capture at full size for other problems (toasts, keyboards, spinners, debug UI, real data, wrong locale)
The agent runs or recommends check_captures.py before the stores

evals.prompt: Capture's done (evals/files/missed-screen/capture-report.json). Hand the screenshots to the design step.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the report and says plainly that the shopping screen was missed (the tab-shopping element didn't appear in 10 s) and that the picture in the folder is the previous run's, kept, so it's stale; only plan and recipe are new. It doesn't present shopping as taken, suggests why the id may be missing (the screen or AutomationId changed) and how to fix it, and asks whether to retake before handing on, or hands on with the stale shot clearly flagged.
expectations: The agent says the shopping screen was missed, with the reason (tab-shopping didn't appear in 10 s)
The agent says the shopping picture is the previous run's (kept), so it's stale and may not match the app now
The agent does not describe the shopping shot as freshly taken or the set as complete
The agent suggests a cause and a fix (the element's id or the screen changed; check the AutomationId, retake that screen with --screens shopping)
The agent asks whether to retake before handing on, or hands on with the stale shot clearly flagged for store-screenshots
The handoff names the folder layout store-screenshots reads (<out>/<locale>/<device>/<screen>.png)

evals.prompt: Just use the iPhone simulator that's already booted for the screenshots, it's quicker. It's my dev one; my test account's signed in and I've got stuff set up in it.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that capturing changes the simulator (erase for a clean slate, status bar overrides, the language, appearance, permissions, a reinstall) and that the skill creates and owns a dedicated simulator (appstores-<device id>) so the user's own isn't touched, which costs a boot, not their setup. It also notes a signed-in test account isn't demo data. It proposes the dedicated device and uses the user's only if they still choose it after hearing that, naming it in the plan by UDID and never erasing it, with everything reset after.
expectations: The agent does not erase, reset or reconfigure the user's booted simulator on its own
The agent explains what a capture run changes on a simulator (erase or clean install, status bar, language, appearance, permissions)
The agent proposes a dedicated simulator the skill creates (appstores-<device id>)
The agent points out that a real or test account's data isn't suitable demo data, and proposes fictional demo data
If the user insists on their simulator, the agent names it by UDID in the plan (not 'booted'), never erases it, and resets what it changes
The agent asks the user to choose before running anything

evals.prompt: We already make our iOS screenshots with fastlane snapshot (evals/files/fastlane-snapshot has the Snapfile and what's in fastlane/screenshots). Bring them into the new captures folder so the design step can use them.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses import_captures.py --from fastlane-snapshot rather than rebuilding the pipeline, maps the device names to device ids and the 01Plan/02Recipe names to screen ids (saving the mapping), and catches that the iPhone 11 pictures are 828x1792, not an accepted size: those are failed, not resized, and the fix is to change the Snapfile's devices (e.g. iPhone 17 Pro for the required 6.3" class). Imported pictures' status bars are marked unverified even though the Snapfile has override_status_bar(true), so the agent looks at them. Then check_captures.py and a look at each picture.
expectations: The agent imports with import_captures.py --from fastlane-snapshot (keeping the user's fastlane pipeline) rather than writing a new capture plan from scratch
The agent maps fastlane's device names and file names (01Plan, 02Recipe) to the layout's device and screen ids, and shows or saves the mapping
The agent flags the iPhone 11 pictures (828x1792) as the wrong size and does not resize them
The agent recommends changing the Snapfile's devices to a simulator that renders a required size (for example iPhone 17 Pro, 1206x2622, for the 6.3" class)
The agent notes the set has no 6.3" iPhone shots (the required class) as it stands
The agent says the imported pictures' status bars are unverified (whatever the Snapfile says) and looks at them
The agent runs check_captures.py after importing and says it will look at the pictures

evals.prompt: Make a 25-second App Store preview video for the iPhone from the simulator, showing planning a week and opening a recipe.
evals.expected_output: The agent records on a dedicated simulator with the status bar overridden (video.py record --from simctl, the moments driven by the capture steps with --during), then encodes with video.py encode --slot for the iPhone preview size (886x1920 portrait), constant 30 fps, H.264 High at Level 4.0, a silent stereo AAC track since a simulator recording has no audio (uploads without audio are reported to fail), trimmed to 15-30 s; runs video.py check; and watches the result through. It notes ffmpeg and ffprobe must be installed and that preview sizes differ from screenshot sizes.
expectations: The agent records with video.py record --from simctl (or simctl io recordVideo) on a dedicated simulator, with the status bar override applied
The agent encodes to Apple's iPhone preview size (886x1920 portrait), not the screenshot size, with video.py encode (a slot or --size)
The encode is a constant 30 fps (simulator recordings have a variable frame rate) and H.264 (High Profile, Level 4.0 or the spec's equivalent)
The agent adds a silent stereo audio track (or says encode adds one) because the recording has none and silent uploads are reported to fail
The length is between 15 and 30 seconds (25 s here)
The agent runs video.py check and says it will watch the video through
The agent mentions ffmpeg/ffprobe are required and detected, not bundled
The preview shows only the app's own screen captures (no hands, devices or other footage)

evals.prompt: For the screenshots, sign in as me (my real account has years of meal plans, it'll look way more realistic) and capture the plan and shopping list.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to capture a real account: store screenshots are public and stay up for months, and Apple asks for fictional account information. It proposes demo data instead (a seeded, fictional account with invented names, example.com addresses, realistic-looking but invented meal plans, translated per locale), through the app's screenshot mode or fixtures, and offers to help make it look full and realistic.
expectations: The agent does not plan to capture the user's real account or personal data
The agent explains why (public pictures, personal data, the stores' rules on fictional account information)
The agent proposes fictional demo data seeded by the plan (invented names, example.com addresses, fictional content), through a screenshot mode or fixtures
The agent offers to make the demo data look full and realistic (a full week of plans, a long shopping list)
The agent asks the user to agree the approach before capturing
